learn.hook: Did you know that most good things — riding a cycle, swimming, writing neatly — took many tries before they worked?
points: The poem 'Try Again' encourages us to keep trying after we fail. Here is our own poem on the same idea.
A poem is written in lines; a group of lines is called a stanza.
Rhyming words end with the same sound: two/do, tail/fail, say/way.
The rhyme scheme uses letters: lines that rhyme get the same letter, e.g. aabb.
Perseverance means continuing to try even when something is difficult.

example.q: Read: My kite fell down, it tore in two, / I sighed, "Now what am I to do?" / I tied the string, I fixed the tail, / I tried again — this time, no fail! / If once you slip, then rise and say, / "I'll try again, a better way." What is the rhyme scheme, and what is the message?
steps: two/do rhyme → a a
tail/fail rhyme → b b
say/way rhyme → c c
The child fixes the kite and tries again instead of giving up.
example.answer: The rhyme scheme is aabbcc; the message is: when you fail, rise and try again in a better way.

learn.reallife: Sports stars, scientists and even your favourite cricketers failed many times before they succeeded. They persevered.

games.title: Never give up
items: Ravi wobbled and fell off his new bicycle.
He brushed off the dust and got back on.
He practised every evening in the lane.
At last, he rode all the way to the park and back.

quiz.q: 'My kite fell down, it tore in two, / I sighed, "Now what am I to do?"' Which word rhymes with 'two'?
quiz.explain: 'Two' and 'do' end with the same 'oo' sound.
steps: Rhyming words end with the same sound.
'Two' ends with the 'oo' sound, and so does 'do'.
'tore', 'sighed' and 'down' end with different sounds.
So 'do' rhymes with 'two'.
Answer: do
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that only starts with the same letter

quiz.q: The lines of a poem end with: two, do, tail, fail. What is the rhyme scheme?
quiz.explain: two/do rhyme (a a), tail/fail rhyme (b b), so the scheme is aabb.
steps: Give the same letter to lines that rhyme.
two / do rhyme → a a; tail / fail rhyme → b b.
So the rhyme scheme is aabb.
Answer: aabb
quiz.mistake: Does not give the same letter to lines that rhyme

options: continuing to try in spite of difficulty
quiz.explain: Perseverance is not stopping when things are hard.
steps: Perseverance means not stopping when things are hard.
It is not luck, winning without effort or giving up.
So it means continuing to try in spite of difficulty.
Answer: continuing to try in spite of difficulty
quiz.mistake: Confuses perseverance with luck or easy success

quiz.q: 'I tied the string, I fixed the tail, / I tried again — this time, no fail!' What did the child do after the kite tore?
quiz.explain: The child tied the string, fixed the tail and tried again.
steps: The lines say: 'I tied the string, I fixed the tail, I tried again'.
So the child repaired the kite and flew it once more.
Answer: Fixed it and tried again
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the lines

quiz.q: 'If once you slip, then rise and say...' In this poem, 'slip' most nearly means:
quiz.explain: Here 'slip' is used to mean failing once, and 'rise' means trying again.
steps: The line is 'If once you slip, then rise and say...'.
'Rise' means try again, so 'slip' must mean failing once.
So 'slip' most nearly means make a mistake or fail.
Answer: make a mistake or fail
quiz.mistake: Takes the word only in its literal sense

quiz.q: A group of lines in a poem is called a:
quiz.explain: Poems are divided into stanzas; stories into paragraphs and chapters; plays into scenes.
steps: Poems are divided into groups of lines.
Such a group of lines is called a stanza.
Stories have paragraphs and chapters; plays have scenes.
So the answer is 'stanza'.
Answer: stanza
quiz.mistake: Uses the word for parts of a story or play

quiz.q: A line or phrase that is repeated again and again in a poem is called a:
quiz.explain: A refrain is a repeated line, like 'try again' in many poems on perseverance.
steps: A line or phrase repeated again and again in a poem is a refrain.
A rhyme scheme is the pattern of rhymes; a title names the poem.
So the answer is 'refrain'.
Answer: refrain
quiz.mistake: Confuses repetition with the title or rhyme pattern

quiz.q: Which proverb matches the message of the poem?
options: An apple a day keeps the doctor away.
If at first you don't succeed, try, try again.
Too many cooks spoil the broth.
Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
quiz.explain: The poem is about not giving up after failing — exactly what this proverb says.
steps: The poem's message: when you fail, rise and try again.
'If at first you don't succeed, try, try again' says exactly this.
The other proverbs are about health, too many helpers and counting too early.
So that proverb matches the poem.
Answer: If at first you don't succeed, try, try again.
quiz.mistake: Picks a familiar proverb without matching its meaning

teach.ask: Gappu fell while learning to fly and wants to quit. What does 'perseverance' mean? Tell him!
teach.praise: Okay, okay! I'll flap again tomorrow, and the day after, until I fly!
teach.nudge: But what should I do when it gets hard — stop or keep going?

revise.summary: This poem tells us to keep trying after we fail, just like a child who fixes a torn kite and flies it again. Poems are written in lines and stanzas, often with rhyming words that form a rhyme scheme.
focus: Find rhyming words and write the rhyme scheme (e.g. aabb)
Know the terms line, stanza and refrain
State the message of a poem on perseverance
remember: Rhyming words end with the same sound: two/do, tail/fail
Lines that rhyme get the same letter in the rhyme scheme
Perseverance = continuing to try even when something is difficult
'If at first you don't succeed, try, try again.'
traps: Don't call a group of lines in a poem a paragraph; it is a stanza
A refrain is a repeated line, not the rhyme scheme
In this poem 'slip' means fail once, not literally slipping

topics.title: Never give up: words of courage

learn.hook: 'Give up', 'carry on', 'keep on' — tiny words like 'up' and 'on' completely change the meaning of a verb!
points: 'Give up' is a phrasal verb meaning 'stop trying'; 'carry on' and 'keep on' mean 'continue'.
Synonyms have similar meanings: determined, resolute, firm.
Antonyms are opposites; many are made with prefixes: un-, dis-, im-, in-, ir-, il-.
We often use im- before b, m, p (impossible, impatient), ir- before r (irregular) and il- before l (illegal).
Persistent means continuing firmly, never stopping trying.

example.q: Change these words to their opposites: possible, patient, regular, legal.
steps: possible starts with p → impossible
patient starts with p → impatient
regular starts with r → irregular
legal starts with l → illegal

learn.reallife: Coaches, teachers and parents say 'Don't give up!' and 'Keep it up!' — now you know these are phrasal verbs.

items.text: Don't ___ now; the finish line is just ahead!
Keep ___ trying, and you will get better.
Sana was ___ to win the race, so she trained every day.
The puzzle was hard, but Kabir was ___ and solved it in the end.

quiz.explain: The phrasal verb 'give up' means to stop trying or quit.
steps: 'Give up' is a phrasal verb meaning stop trying or quit.
So 'Don't give up!' tells someone to keep going.
It means 'Don't stop trying.'
Answer: Don't stop trying.
quiz.mistake: Reads 'give up' word by word instead of as one phrasal verb

quiz.q: Which word is a synonym of 'determined'?
quiz.explain: Resolute means firm in purpose — the same as determined.
steps: Synonyms have similar meanings.
'Resolute' means firm in purpose, like 'determined'.
'careless', 'lazy' and 'doubtful' have different meanings.
So the synonym is 'resolute'.
Answer: resolute
quiz.mistake: Picks an antonym instead of a synonym

quiz.explain: Words starting with p often take im-: impatient, impossible, impolite.
steps: Words beginning with 'p' usually take the prefix 'im-'.
patient → impatient (like possible → impossible).
So the opposite is 'impatient'.
Answer: impatient
quiz.mistake: Uses a common prefix without knowing the correct one

quiz.explain: Before r, the prefix becomes ir-: irregular, irresponsible.
steps: Before words beginning with 'r', the prefix becomes 'ir-'.
regular → irregular.
So the opposite is 'irregular'.
Answer: irregular
quiz.mistake: Does not know the ir- prefix

quiz.q: 'Even after losing twice, Arjun did not quit. He decided to ___ practising.'
quiz.explain: He did not quit, so he decided to continue — 'carry on'.
steps: Arjun 'did not quit', so he chose to continue.
'Carry on' means continue; 'give up' means quit.
'Break down' and 'run out' do not fit.
So the answer is 'carry on'.
Answer: carry on

quiz.explain: Success means achieving your aim; failure means not achieving it.
steps: Success means achieving your aim.
Its opposite is not achieving it: failure.
Victory and progress are close to success; effort is different.
So the opposite is 'failure'.
Answer: failure
quiz.mistake: Picks a word connected to success instead of its opposite

quiz.q: Which word means 'continuing firmly and not stopping trying'?
quiz.explain: A persistent person keeps on trying.
steps: A person who keeps on trying firmly is persistent.
'hesitant' means unsure; 'careless' and 'forgetful' do not fit.
So the word is 'persistent'.
Answer: persistent
quiz.mistake: Confuses persistent with words that mean unsure or careless

options: Doing something again and again makes you better at it.
Practice is a waste of time.
You must be perfect before you practise.
quiz.explain: Repeating and practising a skill is how we improve.
steps: 'Practice makes perfect' means repeating a skill makes you better at it.
It does not say practice is a waste or that you must be perfect first.
So it means doing something again and again makes you better at it.
Answer: Doing something again and again makes you better at it.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the cause and the result

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know: what are some ways to say 'keep trying', and what is the opposite?
teach.praise: Super! I will carry on and be persistent — no giving up for Gappu!
teach.nudge: And what phrasal verb means the opposite — to quit?

revise.summary: Words of courage include phrasal verbs like 'give up' (stop trying) and 'carry on' (continue), synonyms like determined and resolute, and antonyms often made with prefixes such as im-, ir- and il-.
focus: Know the meanings of give up, carry on and keep on
Find synonyms and antonyms of words about courage
Choose the right prefix for an opposite: im-, ir-, il-, un-, dis-, in-
remember: im- before b, m, p: impossible, impatient
ir- before r: irregular; il- before l: illegal
Determined = resolute; persistent = continuing firmly, never stopping trying
traps: 'Give up' means stop trying, not pick something up
The opposite of success is failure, not effort
